annotation.method: Codex read the complete 20-page local paper sequentially, surveyed every section, order-condition table, method construction, numerical study, conclusion, declaration, and reference, visually checked all three selected source pages, searched all 24 frozen mounted object modules, and compiled private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P18 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; Journal of Scientific Computing 92, article 6, 2022, pages 1-20

rejected_candidates.reason: These introduce standard Runge--Kutta notation and motivate the mixed-precision midpoint method; the convergence plot is empirical. The selected targets use the paper's derived error framework.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the full consistency and perturbation condition lists (3.4) and (3.5) beyond order two
rejected_candidates.reason: The higher-order catalogs require a substantial rooted-tree and differentiability interface. T2 uses only the exact order-two subset instantiated by the corrected midpoint arrays, while T3 addresses the higher-order Method 4s3pC construction.

rejected_candidates.candidate: low-precision and naive mixed-precision midpoint error forms in Section 3.2
rejected_candidates.reason: Their O(Δt²)+O(ε) and O(Δt²)+O(εΔt) patterns are earlier, weaker instances of the correction progression represented by T2.

rejected_candidates.candidate: corrected SDIRK and Lobatto IIIC constructions (4.5) and (4.8)
rejected_candidates.reason: They repeat the correction-order mechanism with larger coefficient arrays. The corrected midpoint result gives a cleaner T2, while Method 4s3pC supplies the distinct two-regime T3.
The decimal coefficient tables and stability classifications would require separate exact coefficient certificates and a Runge--Kutta stability interface absent from the frozen library.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Figures 2-6 and their numerical convergence discussions
rejected_candidates.reason: These are finite experiments illustrating the derived asymptotic orders, not universally quantified mathematical results.

rejected_candidates.candidate: stability, efficiency, and varying-epsilon directions in Section 5
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper explicitly identifies rigorous stability analysis, efficiency studies, and varying epsilon as limitations or future work rather than completed results.

T1.decision: Use the exact unnumbered E = E_sch + E_per statement after equation (3.3) over an arbitrary real state module. Link it to the original additive outputs (3.1), avoiding the inconsistent sign rewrite in (3.2), expose the exact output difference, and retain Euclidean triangle inequality only after an arbitrary additive observation into finite coordinates.

T2.decision: Use the exact corrected-midpoint Butcher arrays after equation (4.1), together with their order-two consistency conditions and the smooth and nonsmooth perturbation cancellations from (3.4)-(3.5). Do not assign exact norm or hidden-constant semantics to the following conditional global big-O expectation.

T3.decision: Use Method 4s3pC's two stability-conditional global error regimes on page 18. Represent the unprinted exact tableau presupposed by the paper's exact order conditions without claiming that the rounded displayed decimals are exact, retain every third-order and smooth perturbation condition, link local errors to executions of algorithm (3.1), state the required finite-time stability property explicitly, and derive the smooth O(h^3)+O(epsilon*h^3) and nonsmooth O(h^3)+O(epsilon*h^2) bounds with existential hidden constants.

selection_policy: Use accuracy results derived in this paper rather than standard Runge--Kutta definitions, numerical plots, or future-work claims.
Do not replace underspecified asymptotic big-O statements with exact norm inequalities; select exact source content or formalize all asymptotic semantics explicitly.
Preserve the paper's distinction between scheme error, smooth perturbation error, and nonsmooth perturbation error.
Keep every public definition free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only from the 24 modules in metadata/library_olean.json.
